List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on

Total number of questions — 20
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Recovery of human skeletons in
Noida
†*121. SHRI SATYAVRAT
CHATURVEDI:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the shocking incident of
recovery of a large number of human
skeletons in December, 2006 from Noida
had come to light;
(b) whether Government are conducting
a CBI inquiry into the incident;
(c) the number of incidents of missing
children that have come to light so far and
the number of FIRs registered by police
from time to time;
(d) the details regarding the number of
persons found guilty;
(e) to which States the missing children
belonged; and
(f) the number of innocent persons
apprehended by police and the action taken
by Government to get them released?
Survey of poor families in rural
areas
†*122. SHRI BRIJ BHUSHAN
TIWARI: Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the poor
people in rural areas of Chhattisgarh,
Orissa, Madhya Pradesh and some other
States are making both their ends meet by
daily earning of Rs. 9 to Rs. 12 only;
(b) whether any survey has been
conducted in relation to everyday living of
the poor families in rural areas of these
States;
(c) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor; and
(d) the steps Government are taking to
improve the living standard of the poor of
the rural areas in those States?
Notification on Fixed Term
Employment Workmen
*123. SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to refer to
answer to Starred Question 318 given in

41
the Rajya Sabha on the 13th December,
2006 and state:
(a) whether any decision has since been
taken by Government to rescind the
notification dated 10th December, 2003
regarding Fixed Term Employment
Workmen; and
(b) if not, the reasons therefor?
Child trafficking
*124. SHRI DEVDAS APTE: Will the
Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
child trafficking has become a high profitable
business in India;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government are also aware
that this is reported to be happening mainly
in the backward States;
(d) if so, the State-wise details thereof;
and
(e) what action Government have taken
to stop this menace?
Induction of Arjun Tanks
*125. MS. MABEL REBELLO:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of DEFENCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Arjun Tank has been
approved by Indian Army for adoption;
(b) if not, the reasons therefor;
(c) if so, when and how many Arjun
Tanks have been inducted so far in Indian
Army;
(d) whether the Indian Army has placed
further orders for Arjun Tank; and
(e) if so, whether the order is sufficient
to maintain the assembly lines of the Tank?
Missing persons in J & K
*126. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
SHRI AMAR SINGH:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
a large number of innocent people from
J&K who are reported to have been missing
during the last several years are alleged to
have been killed by the Army/CRPF;
(b) if so, what are the details of the
missing persons in J&K during the last three
years; and
(c) whether it is a fact that Special
Investigating Team, probing the fake
encounters killings in J&K, has recently
exhumed a few bodies from graveyards and
if so, the details thereof and the action taken
against the officers concerned?
Cases registered for protection of
Civil Rights Act and SC/ST
(Prevention of Atrocities) Act
*127. SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) the number of cases registered under
the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
during last three years, State-wise;
(b) the number of cases registered under
the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act,
1989 during the same period, State-wise;
(c) whether it is a fact that there is a
huge gap between the cases registered under
the two Acts; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor?

Restriction on movement of 12th Tai
Situpa of Tibet
*128. SHRI NABAM REBIA: Will the
Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that certain
restrictions on the movement of His
Eminence the 12th Tai Situpa of Kagyu
lineage of the Tibetan Buddhism in India
and abroad have been imposed by
Government;
(b) whether any recognized political/
social/religious forum has approached
Government for lifting such restrictions to
enable him to perform his religious/spiritual
duties;
(c) whether Government are aware that
such restrictions on the movement of a
highly learned scholar and internationally
recognized profound teacher of Dharma is
resented by thousands of his followers in
India and abroad; and
(d) specific reasons for such
restrictions?
Uniform rates for cable subscribers
*129. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH: Will
the Minister of INFORMATION AND
BROADCASTING be pleased to state:
(a) whether his Ministry has received
any proposal from the Government of
Andhra Pradesh to fix uniform rate to be
charged from the customers by cable
operators in the metros, district
headquarters and rural areas, to fix the
entertainment tax to be charged on cable
operators and to set up a competent
authority for collecting entertainment tax;
(b) if so, the response of the Ministry
thereto; and
(c) the details of steps taken on the above
said proposal?
Payments to shareholders of Swadesi
Cotton Mills, Kanpur
†*130. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN:
Will the Minister of TEXTILES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are committed
to make payment to shareholders of
Swadesi Cotton Mills, Kanpur;
(b) if so, the method of making payment
to such shareholders;
(c) the number of shareholders who have
been made payments so far;
(d) the number of shareholders who are
yet to receive their payment; and
(e) by when Government would make
payment to small shareholders under IV
and V categories so that their interests are
well taken care of?
Missing children in the country
*131. SHRI MOTIUR RAHMAN:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) the total number of children gone
missing during the last three years,
State-wise/Union Territory-wise and
year-wise;
(b) how many of the missing children
have been traced and the reasons for not
recovering the remaining children;
(c) whether Government are aware that
some groups are involved in kidnapping/
selling of children;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the action taken to banish such
groups/gangs?

Training for Orissa police personnel
*132. SHRI B.J. PANDA:
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Orissa Chief Minister
has made a request to the Centre for
imparting basic training to about 3000 State
police personnel, in Central Para Military
training institutions, to help them curb naxal
menace;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) what is the status of this request
indicating the time-frame within which the
help asked for would be provided to the
State?
Criteria for setting up of EOUs
†*133. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to state:
(a) the criteria fixed by Government for
setting up of Export-Oriented Units;
(b) whether any efforts have been made
to promote setting up of export-oriented
units; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Assistance to handloom weavers
*134. KUMARI NIRMALA
DESHPANDE: Will the Minister of
TEXTILES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the handloom
weavers of Pochampalli village near
Hyderabad, known for their skills, are in
distress today;
(b) if so, what steps are being taken to
help them; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Re-examining of SEZ scheme
*135. SHRI SHANTARAM
LAXMAN NAIK:
SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government of India
are re-examining the policy and the law
governing Special Economic Zones;
(b) whether the establishment of SEZs
is kept on hold;
(c) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(d) the steps taken by the Ministry for
early implementation of the SEZ scheme?
Funding routes of terrorists
*136. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
SHRI K.E. ISMAIL:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the terrorists funding routes in the country
through stock exchanges, banking channels,
ordinary ATM withdrawals and hawala
trails, as well as operation of legitimate
business like hotels and transport;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) what steps are being taken by
Government to check such terror
fundings?

Development of infrastructure in
textile sector
*137. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister of TEXTILES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is
ambitious programme to develop
infrastructure in the textile sector;
(b) if so, the details thereof and whether
it will generate employment opportunities
which is becoming operational;
(c) whether Centre will totally take care
of financial aspect; and
(d) whether on its fully functional,
Government would be able to earn foreign
exchange?
Facilities for economic growth at
borders
*138. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that, in its attempt
to integrate foreign policy with trade, India
will make it easier for its neighbours to log
into its economic growth at its borders;
(b) whether the Cabinet has approved
an elaborate plan to establish a Land Ports
Authority of India (LPAI) and 13 State-of-
the-art Integrated Check Posts (ICPs) on
the Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal and
Pakistan borders; and
(c) if so, the details thereof and the
estimated cost of new proposed
infrastructure project?
Child labour
*139. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that instances of child labour are
continuing in the country, despite a ban on
it;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that the National
Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has
issued notices to Delhi Government in this
regard;
(d) whether Government have any
mechanism for proper monitoring of
implementation of the ban;
(e) if so, the details thereof; and
(f) the details of steps taken to
effectively curb child labour?

countries from which they were received,
in each case?
